articles.title: Cs Orange Navy
articles.summary: Dark brown base with faint blue and purple marbled blotches, low contrast, satin with medium sparkle. Reads as a vivid teal and purple marbled swirl, busy and watery, with the bands blurring into a shifting two-tone shimmer.
articles.what: Up close: Dense contour-line moire: wavy bands about 8 to 12 px wide in teal and violet, flowing in parallel sweeps at the upper left and breaking into twisty loops, whorls and eddies toward the centre, like fingerprints or water interference. A third blue-indigo shade shows in the gaps. From a distance: Reads as a vivid teal and purple marbled swirl, busy and watery, with the bands blurring into a shifting two-tone shimmer. Measured spec (average): metal 110, roughness 77, coat 145. Shine: satin. Metal: medium. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: dirt late model, truck / off-road, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Cs Orange Navy" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood and roof: wide panels show the flow and whorls
Whole body for the full marble effect; keep numbers on a plate
Very busy: numbers need a solid plate with a thick outline; small numbers vanish in the contours.
Nothing busy: the ripples are already the design
Pairs well with: orange, cream, copper, black.
pitfalls: Not a smooth gradient: it is fine contour bands, so it looks busy
Not carbon or weave: no regular grid, the lines flow organically
Avoid: dark numbers on the dark base, big flat dark areas in the sim.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 110 (pearl-level metal), roughness 77 (satin gloss), clearcoat 145 (dull or trace clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: dark numbers on the dark base, big flat dark areas in the sim.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: nothing busy: the ripples are already the design; a solid plate for numbers and logos: the contours cut through small text
Patterns to avoid: stripes, camo, grids or weave: moire against the bands; other loud colour-shift or glitter patterns: stack too much
